title: A rectangle corner used as T can leave its side; the touching circle then touches nothing, and its touching point is reported off the curve
detail: onCurveByRefs counts a rectangle's handle a or b as on side `part` when it is a corner of that side at pick time. A rectangle re-sorts its corners from min/max, so dragging b across a moves corner a to other sides, while the curve ref keeps its part. touchForm never checks that T is on C, and evalNode still attaches tch = {G: C's form, tp: T}, so meetsOf's touching rule keeps returning T for K ∩ C. onPiece on a segment only checks the projection parameter, so the false point passes. Result: the row says 'touching side 1 of Rectangle 1', the circle does not meet that side at all, and the point 'Circle 1 ∩ side 1 of Rectangle 1, where they touch' sits 1 unit away from the side. The same false meet follows from any saved file where T is not on C.
evidence: node: notes/orthogonal-circle/review-math/t2.js. Rect a=0, b=2+i; T = handle a on side 0; P = 1+2i. Before: K centre 1.25i, r 1.25, meet 0, f_side(meet) = 0. After b -> 2-i: side 0 is y = -1, K is unchanged, the meet stays 0, f_side(meet) = -2, onCurveByRefs is now false, and Constr.meets on the pieces still gives [0, 0]. App (dist/test.html, real drag of handle b, notes/orthogonal-circle/review-math/a2.js, shot notes/orthogonal-circle/review-math/mrv-s2b-after.png): rect [0, 2-i]; K's row 'through z₀, touching side 1 of Rectangle 1 at corner 1 of Rectangle 1'; z₁ = 0 with the row 'Circle 1 ∩ side 1 of Rectangle 1, where they touch'; the circle is visibly 1 unit above the bottom side.
fix: Do both. (1) In evalNode's touch branch, check that T is on C's piece to within rounding, for example |f_C(T)| ≤ 1e-12·S with S as in section F's metric. If it is not, fail with a reason, or at least do not attach tch, so meetsOf solves normally. That also covers crafted saves. (2) In onCurveByRefs, drop rectangle corners, or resolve them per side at evaluation time, because a rectangle's corner-to-side map is not invariant under handle drags. Add a section F test: rect a as T, drag b across a.

title: Use complement on a touching circle turns over a perpendicular circle built on it, and moves gliders on that circle
detail: The perp branch of evalNode undoes C's flip only for circle3 and perp (constr.js:1665). The touch and tangent branch uses ['circle3', 'perp', 'touch', 'tangent'] (constr.js:1692). Touch was added after perp, and the perp line was not widened. A touching circle has Use complement (isCirc3), and perpForm is linear in C's row, so toggling the touching circle's flip negates K. K's region becomes the outside, and the glider map (anchored with sg = K's own flip) runs backwards, so every glider on K jumps to another point. This breaks SPEC 2's 'Use complement on C never turns K over'.
evidence: node: notes/orthogonal-circle/review-math/t1.js. C = unit circle; K = touch(C, glider t=0.1, 2+0.5i); Q = perp(K, 1.5-0.3i, 0.4+1.7i), Region; glider g on Q at t=0.3. Toggle K.def.flip: Q's A goes from +0.5789 to -0.5789, and g moves from (0.3469, 1.7182) to (-0.3998, -1.6393). A touching circle built on K is unaffected. App (notes/orthogonal-circle/review-math/a1.js, shot notes/orthogonal-circle/review-math/mrv-s1-after.png, ⋯ Region then ⋯ Use complement on K): Q's row goes from 'the disc through z₂ and z₃, perpendicular to Circle 2' to 'outside the circle through z₂ and z₃, perpendicular to Disc 1'; g moves the same way.
fix: constr.js:1665: use the same list as 1692, for example a shared const FLIPPED_OPS = ['circle3', 'perp', 'touch', 'tangent']. Add to section E: perp on a touching circle, then Use complement on it; K's form and its gliders are unchanged.

title: Symmetric points (the pencil) are recognised only when P* is exact in binary; decimal mirror pairs give an arbitrary circle chosen by rounding
detail: The pencil test is an exact zero test on the doubles (constr.js:1859). With grid-snapped decimals, P* is almost never a double. So the result is whichever member of the pencil the rounding picks, with no reason shown. For a tilted line C: sometimes a circle centred on C, sometimes the circle on PQ as a diameter, sometimes the line PQ, sometimes another circle, and sometimes undefined. For a circle C, the [math-3] decimal rule turns every decimal pencil into the line through the centre, while the binary-exact 0.5 and 2 give the 'symmetric points' reason. So one configuration has three outcomes, depending on how the decimals round.
evidence: node: notes/orthogonal-circle/review-math/t4.js, t9.js. Unit circle: 0.5 & 2 -> undef pencil; 0.2 & 5, 0.1 & 10, 0.4 & 2.5, 0.1+0.2i & 2+4i -> the line through 0. Line through 0 and 1+2i (y = 2x), mirror pairs on the grid: -0.1+0.3i & 0.3+0.1i -> circle c≈0, r=0.316; 0.5 & -0.3+0.4i -> circle c=0.1+0.2i, r=0.447; 0.7-0.1i & -0.5+0.5i -> circle c=0.55+1.1i, r=1.21; 0.5i & 0.4+0.3i -> line; -0.5+1.5i & 1.5+0.5i -> undef pencil. Real axis, 0.1+0.2i & 0.1-0.2i -> undef pencil (negation is exact).
fix: Add a decimal pencil rule next to [math-3], using the same decimal strings orientD uses. Circle C (c, r): orientD(c, P, Q) = 0 and (P - c)·(Q - c) = r² exactly in decimals. Line C through a, b: dotD(Q - P, b - a) = 0 and orientD(a, b, (P + Q)/2) = 0. When it holds, return {undef: 'pencil'}. Or decide to always draw the line through the centre, and do the same for 0.5 and 2. Either way, one configuration should give one outcome.

title: Perpendicular to a tilted line, with P and Q on a decimal perpendicular: a circle of radius ~4e15, its half-plane side picked by rounding, labelled 'disc', and the far crossing finite
detail: SPEC 2 leaves the decimal line case of a line C unbuilt, saying 'only the tooltip equation differs'. More than that differs. (a) At creation, flip = (A < 0) picks the disc of a ~1e16 circle, so the visible half-plane is set by the sign of the rounding. In about 43% of grid cases it is the opposite of the exact-line rule (left of P → Q). (b) With Region, the row reads 'the disc through z₀ and z₁, perpendicular to Line 1', and the export caption uses the disc template, where the exact case reads 'the half-plane left of z₄ → z₅'. The Inspector shows r = 4229549062302123. (c) K ∩ C's second crossing is a finite point at about 8e15, not ∞, and whether it is index 0 or 1 depends on the rounding. (A grid perpendicular to an axis-parallel line is exact; the tilted case is the one that fails.)
evidence: node: notes/orthogonal-circle/review-math/t3.js. C = line through 0 and 1+2i; 132 grid pairs on perpendiculars: 31 exact lines and 101 circles (rounding). The interior is left of P→Q in 75 cases and right in 57. App (notes/orthogonal-circle/review-math/a1.js scene 3, shot notes/orthogonal-circle/review-math/mrv-s3.png): P = -0.5+0.3i, Q = -0.3+0.2i gives kind 'disc', c = (-1.89e15, -3.78e15), r = 4229549062302123, the row 'the disc through z₀ and z₁, perpendicular to Line 1', and the meet 'Disc 1 ∩ Line 1, first point' at (-3.78e15, -7.57e15). The binary-exact twin (P = -0.5+0.25i, Q = -0.25+0.125i) gives 'the half-plane left of z₄ → z₅'.
fix: Add the decimal rule for a line C. When Gc.A === 0, and the curve piece's decimal endpoints a, b give dotD(Q - P, b - a) = 0 (the decimal analogue of orientD), set a = 0 and B = sn·J(Q - P)/|Q - P|, with sn from the rounded cross product, as the circle-C rule at constr.js:1863 does. The creation flip then follows the left-of-P→Q rule, the far meet is ∞, and the row and caption say line or half-plane. Add the 132-case grid to section E.

title: Use complement on a perpendicular or touching circle swaps its Intersect points with other curves (inherited from circle3)
detail: Meets use the entering rule on the oriented forms. Use complement flips K's form, so index 0 and index 1 of K ∩ D trade places for every curve D. A point the user made with Intersect jumps to the other crossing. SPEC 1.4 protected gliders on K from Use complement, but not meets. The behaviour is the same for circle3 in v16.2, so it is not new. The new tools inherit it: perp K ∩ C and K ∩ any line, and a touching circle ∩ any curve other than C. K ∩ C itself is safe, because the touching rule gives T for both indices.
evidence: node: notes/orthogonal-circle/review-math/t8.js. perp K over the unit circle: K∩C index 0 goes from (0.8808, -0.4735) to (0.2740, 0.9617), and K∩line index 0 from (0.2442, 0.4122) to (2.7090, 0.5355). circle3 gives the same swap in v16.3 and in v16.2's frozen constr.js.
fix: Optional, and as one change for circle3, perp and touch: evaluate a meet's entering rule on the unflipped form (keep pc.G0 for flipped ops, and use it in meetsOf), or swap the stored index when def.flip toggles (one undo step). If it is deferred, record it as a known limitation next to SPEC 1.4.

title: Checked and holding
detail: Continuity sweeps of 4000 steps, measured in the chordal metric. Perp: P across C, C's centre across PQ, C's radius from 0.05 to 3, Q once round P (the line case twice), a line C with Q round P, a line C rotating, a flattening arc C, and a circle3 C through its line case. In every sweep there were no undefined frames, no swaps of K ∩ C, the largest meet step was ≤ 8.8e-3, and the largest glider step was ≤ 4.5e-3. Touch: T once round C, P across C, P orbiting, and C's radius sweep. The meets and gliders are continuous, with jumps only at true tangencies of K with a third line (square-root speed). The tangents' touching points are continuous until P enters C. Save, validate, reload and recompute of a chain (circle3 with flip → perp → glider → touch → tangent → meets) is bitwise identical and idempotent. The tangent's left/right labels do not depend on C's orientation (checked algebraically). Images in Y use Region.formOf and sampleMR on s._g, so huge radii map exactly.
